paper_type_evidence.quote: This work includes 1.3 mm observations of the system RW Aur from several different ALMA projects

evidence.quote: The RW Aur system is composed of at least two stars located at 154 pc away from us (cite: gaia2016b; gaia2021edr3), each hosting its own disk
The RW Aur system is composed of at least two stars located at 154 pc away from us (cite: gaia2016b; gaia2021edr3), each hosting its own disk

question.value: Nature (bound or unbound) of the RW Aur binary interaction and its impact on the dust and gas of the two disks, from multi-epoch 1.3 mm ALMA data

evidence.quote: Thus, the present work aims to study the nature and impact of the binary interaction in the distribution of the gas and dust emission in the individual disks.
In order to constrain the impact and nature of the binary interaction in the RW Aur system (bound or unbound), we analyzed the circumstellar material at 1.3 mm wavelengths

claims.hypothesis: Is the RW Aur binary bound (elliptical orbit) or unbound (hyperbolic fly-by)?
claims.experiment: MCMC orbit fit to ALMA disk-center astrometry, historical astrometry and one ALMA radial velocity, plus AIC comparison and fits without ALMA astrometry
claims.result: Highest-likelihood solutions have ecc 0.5 to 0.95; hyperbolic tail allowed; hyperbolic best models 0.28 times as likely (~1.1 sigma preference for elliptical)
claims.finding: Most likely a high-eccentricity bound orbit with last periastron about 295 yr ago, but hyperbolic orbits are not ruled out

evidence.quote: we constrain the RW Aur binary stars to be most likely in a high-eccentricity elliptical orbit with a clockwise prograde orientation relative to RW Aur A, although low-eccentricity hyperbolic orbits are not ruled out by the astrometry

claims.hypothesis: Can multi-epoch ALMA visibility modeling detect the relative motion of the two disks?
claims.experiment: Joint visibility fit of five epochs with per-epoch disk centers
claims.result: RW Aur B moves toward the southwest relative to A at about 3 mas/yr
claims.finding: A consistent relative motion is detected in ALMA astrometry

evidence.quote: we find a consistent trend of movement for the disk of RW Aur B moving away from the disk of RW Aur A at an approximate rate of 3 mas yr$^{-1}$

claims.hypothesis: Does the inner disk of RW Aur A show a warp from the close interaction?
claims.experiment: Visibility fit allowing the central Gaussian a separate inclination and PA
claims.result: Inner component is 6.0+/-0.4 deg more inclined; peak residual falls from 6 to 5 sigma
claims.finding: A tentative 6 deg warp in the inner 3 au, consistent with the recent interaction

evidence.quote: Evidence for the close interaction is found in a tentative warp of 6 deg in the inner 3 au of the disk of RW Aur A, in the brightness temperature of both disks, and in the morphology of the gas emission.

claims.hypothesis: How large and compact are the two dust disks?
claims.experiment: Parametric visibility modeling of the LB1-dominated continuum
claims.result: R90% = 19 au (A) and 14 au (B); B has a ring at about 6.5 au
claims.finding: Both disks are compact; B shows a narrow ring

evidence.quote: the radius enclosing 90% of the flux ($R_{90\%}$) is 19 au and 14 au for RW Aur A and B, respectively

claims.hypothesis: Is the narrow ring around RW Aur B due to material captured from RW Aur A's disk?
claims.experiment: Compare ring and low brightness temperature of B with the orbit solutions and literature simulations
claims.result: Ring peaks at about 6 au; B brightness temperature at most 15 K versus 120 K for A
claims.finding: Suggestive of captured material, labeled speculative and untested

evidence.quote: A narrow ring that peaks at 6 au around RW Aur B is suggestive of captured material from the disk around RW Aur A.

referee_caveats_inferred: Orbit constraint rests on a handful of ALMA epochs whose spacing is not monotonic (SB1 to SB4 relative distances), and the paper itself attributes this to possible inner-disk asymmetries
ALMA and Gaia DR3 astrometry disagree by about 6 mas and were never combined, so the final orbit relies on assuming disk centers equal stellar positions
Eddy masses carry tiny formal errors yet set the total mass prior; real systematic uncertainty is larger
Visibility weights across cycles were not standardized as the paper itself later recommends
Warp significance is based on one model comparison with a 6 sigma to 5 sigma residual change and no formal model comparison

products_in_archive.value: Self-calibrated measurement sets and FITS images (with and without JvM) released on Zenodo; raw data are from five ALMA projects

evidence.quote: All the selfcalibrated products, including measurement sets and fits files (with and without JvM correction) are available for download at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.12825068>.

missing_for_reproduction: Self-calibration solution intervals, rounds and CLEAN masks (partly bypassed by the Zenodo self-calibrated products)
MCMC walker counts, steps, bounds, likelihood and weighting for the visibility fit
Historical astrometry values used (only the compilation citation and the two excluded points)
Origin of the parallax and total-mass priors and the radial-velocity measurement method
No analysis code released; only data products
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Roughly 100-300 GB of raw ALMA data for 5 projects and 14 execution blocks (long-baseline LB1 is the largest); a few GB from the Zenodo self-calibrated products
reproducibility.score_reason: Public ALMA projects and Zenodo self-calibrated products plus full model equations and numeric tables, but key MCMC and imaging settings, priors for the orbit fit, and historical astrometry values are missing and no code is released.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data are stated available (ALMA projects and Zenodo products), the visibility-fit and orbit-fit recipes are largely described, and results are numeric tables (disk sizes, fluxes, orbital elements).
